summary: The bill amends PURPA to require states to consider adopting a new standard under which utilities using integrated resource planning must include measures ensuring 10 years of reliable electric supply by maintaining or procuring power from generation facilities that can operate continuously for 30+ days with on-site or contracted fuel, function in emergencies, and provide grid support services.

The new PURPA standard requires utilities to plan for 'reliable generation facilities' capable of 30-day continuous operation with on-site or contracted fuel and severe-weather resilience. This definition inherently favors dispatchable baseload sources (coal, natural gas, nuclear) over intermittent renewables and adds a federal requirement that states must consider in resource planning. The effect is to tilt energy policy toward reliability concerns that can slow or constrain aggressive decarbonization and renewable mandates, producing a moderate pro-conventional-energy tilt on climate/environment issues.
